reviews.one_line_contribution: It measures, for the first time with an intervention anchor, how many retrievals a learned per-item memory score takes to follow a leave-one-out value flip after a manufactured ALFWorld rule change, and shows that the delay is manufactured by co-retrieval: stale items sitting in sets with fresh items keep absorbing credit for successes they did not cause.
reviews.closest_prior_work: RoMeRL (arXiv:2608.02508, verified this session with s2cli paper: 'Balancing Feedback Coverage and the Memory-Reward Trap in Self-Evolving Agent Memory via Reduced-Order Utility States', 2026-08-03). Its abstract names the memory-reward trap and states that reduced-order utility states 'limit persistent reward contamination' - the exact mechanism this proposal calls its headline (co-retrieved items absorbing joint outcome credit) is already named, and a method is already positioned as mitigating it. The proposal's reply, that RoMeRL argues from a coordinate-transition model rather than counterfactual measurement, is correct and is the whole novelty margin: the phenomenon is prior, only the leave-one-out anchor, the manipulated set composition and the lag-in-retrievals metric are new. A reviewer who thinks a measurement of an already-named effect inside one manufactured shim is not an ICLR contribution will not be moved by that margin. Second threat, found by my own search and absent from the proposal: MemStrata (arXiv:2606.26511, 'Temporal Validity in Retrieval Memory', 2026-06-25, cit 4, s2+hf), whose motivating example is literally this proposal's manipulation ('a function is renamed') and which reports that cosine similarity separates a contradicted fact from a duplicated one at AUROC 0.59; it operates at fact level in RAG and never watches a utility score respond, so it threatens the framing, not the claim. Also close and uncited: STALE (arXiv:2605.06527, 'Can LLM Agents Know When Their Memories Are No Longer Valid?', hf) and Memory-R2 (arXiv:2605.21768, verified: 'Fair Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Memory-Augmented LLM Agents', 2026-05-20, cit 5), the latter explicitly about credit under shared memory state, though it optimizes credit rather than measuring it against a counterfactual.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline P2 is close to arithmetic in sign, and its only open content - the factor of 3 - is set by the authors' own free choices. An outcome-reinforced score falls only when episodes fail; mixed sets contain two fresh post-drift items chosen precisely because they rescue the episode, so mixed sets fail less, so the stale item's score decays more slowly there. That is the update rule composed with a success-rate gap the design manufactures. What remains to be measured is a ratio jointly determined by (a) the quality of the fresh pool - the proposal concedes 'flip lag is defined against a fresh-item median, which depends on the fresh pool's quality' - and (b) the scorer's learning rate and decay constant, which are never pinned, never ablated, and belong to the authors' own reimplementations 'from abstracts and method sections'. So '3x' can be moved either way by tuning a constant no published paper fixed, and the claim 'published scorers are slow' is not tested, because no published scorer is run. Compounding this, three of the four non-control predictions are damaged as written: P5's falsifying threshold (+8) sits one point above its own stated MDE (~7), so a true null returns an upper bound of ~7 straddling the boundary and everything from ~1 to 8 net falls into the declared inconclusive zone - and P5 sources itself to 'the D2 mixed interaction block', which does not exist (D2 runs only k=0 and stale-only k=3 at 3 seeds; the mixed block is a D1 cell); P3's pruning threshold is a 25th percentile over a bank dominated by never-retrieved, never-updated items while the stale class was selected for the highest pre-drift retrieval frequency, so '>= 30% retained' is close to guaranteed by the selection rule, and its companion clause ('LOO-anchored <= 5%') follows from that estimator's definition and is given no falsifier at all; P4 averages confidence gain over a trajectory in which the rule change touches one or two command steps out of ten to twenty navigation and pick-up steps the stale item still matches, with no per-step decomposition, so '>= 50% retained' is near-guaranteed by dilution. P1, the gate on which everything else is conditioned, has a falsifier ('CI entirely above -5' at half-width ~5) that requires a positive point estimate, leaving the entire no-harm world between 0 and -5 neither confirming nor falsifying.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Take the scorer hyperparameters out of the result: pre-register the decay/learning-rate grid and report the lag ratio as a function of it, or normalize every lag by the LOO-anchored scorer's lag on the same stream and make that ratio, not raw retrievals, the headline; better still, report accumulated harm in net points during the lag, which the design already collects and which the update rule cannot trivially set. 2) Fix the thresholds: state P1 as 'the 95% CI excludes -10', or run D0 at 4x seeds (half-width ~2.5); run the four mixed cells at enough seeds for MDE ~3.5 and state P5 as a CI excluding +8 with the null two MDEs away; correct the arm reference from D2 to the D1 mixed block. 3) Define P3's threshold over items retrieved since the drift, or as an absolute score calibrated to the fresh class, pre-register the stale class's percentile trajectory under a no-movement null, and give the LOO-anchored clause its own falsifying outcome. 4) Decompose P4's confidence gain into the drifted procedural-command step and the rest, and state the falsifier on the procedural component. 5) Add the cheap-signal baseline below. 6) Consider making the composition manipulation the paper: the removal interaction (P5) is the genuinely new measurement and does not depend on the shim being realistic, whereas every lag number does.
reviews.missing_baseline: An execution-feedback / conflict-signal scorer that costs essentially nothing. This very shim emits 'Nothing happens.' at exactly the step the stale item recommends, so a scorer that credits an item only for steps whose recommended command actually executed - or decrements on an item-attributable failed action - should flip within one or two retrievals at zero extra episodes. The plan's cheapest correct alternative is the LOO-anchored online scorer at 2x episode cost, so the paper's implicit conclusion ('seeing the flip costs 2x') collapses if a free environment signal beats it, and anyone who has read the validity-check line (MemStrata 2606.26511, RaMem 2606.22844, PlanFence 2609.03340) will demand it. Two smaller omissions in D4: no random-pruning and no post-drift-recency-pruning control, so 'score-based pruning retains 30% of stale items' has nothing to be worse than.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. All queries ran on channel (a) s2cli (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace; s2=ok hf=ok on every run); WebSearch was unavailable this session and WebFetch was not used. (i) 'per-item memory utility score lag after environment rule change leave-one-out counterfactual flip' (unrestricted) -> CUE-R 2604.05467 (per-item RAG perturbation, single-shot), 2210.10769 (Shapley attribution of performance change to distribution shift), 2309.14989, 2401.08348; nothing on agent-memory score lag. (ii) 'co-retrieval credit contamination memory items reinforcement stale outdated experience agent' --recent -> Compliance Trap 2607.10608, MemStrata 2606.26511, Memory-R2 2605.21768, HiMPO 2606.16285, TreeMem 2605.04811, MemQ 2605.08374, MemHarness 2607.28272, 2608.04574; credit-splitting methods, none measuring a score's response to a known invalidation. (iii) 'stale memory item value decay LLM agent experience reuse after rule change' --recent -> 2608.04574, MemStrata 2606.26511, TrustMem 2606.25161, 2606.17591, 2604.08706, A-MAC 2603.04549, Zombie Agents 2602.15654. (iv) closest named method, 'strategic forgetting dynamic memory utility survival importance agent memory pruning' -> 2604.02280, FadeMem 2601.18642, REMEMBERER 2306.07929, MemCon 2607.13591; SF-AMS itself did not surface on this phrasing. (v) 'temporal validity superseded fact retrieval agent memory stale value detection' --recent -> 2608.20685 (temporal validity on real software histories), TRACE 2607.00339, MemStrata 2606.26511, STALE 2605.06527, MINTEval 2605.18565, Memora 2604.20006. Every arXiv ID the novelty argument leans on was verified with s2cli paper and matched the proposal's description: 2608.02508 (RoMeRL), 2607.22562 (SF-AMS), 2605.08374 (MemQ), 2604.00131 (Oblivion), 2606.17591 (insight governance), 2609.03340 (PlanFence, 'Fresh Memory, Stale Plans', 2026-09-03), 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap), 2604.20006 (Memora), 2605.18565 (MINTEval), 2608.04574 (spatial staleness), 2604.02280 (forgetting), 2604.21432 (RAW-UCB rotting bandits), 1511.05952 (Prioritized Experience Replay), 2604.08706 (RL training with experience replay); none failed to resolve. Judging the proposal's own check: it is above average for this pipeline - it labels its channel, reports two queries as returning literally nothing rather than papering over them, and verifies one ID with the paper endpoint - but it has one real hole and one real overclaim. The hole: every query is phrased in agent-memory vocabulary, so it never reaches the temporal-validity / supersession cluster that owns this exact manipulation, and therefore misses MemStrata 2606.26511 (motivating example: a renamed function), STALE 2605.06527, 2608.20685 and TRACE 2607.00339, all reachable in one search. The overclaim: 'no paper measures per-item score lag against a leave-one-out flip' is an absence claim resting on five queries, four of them agent-side, while the proposal cites a dozen arXiv IDs in its novelty argument and verifies exactly one.
